e

decision.explanation: The scalar projection is (p·q)/‖q‖. Here p·q = 4(2)+1(3)+4(3)=23 and ‖q‖=√(2²+3²+3²)=√22, so the answer is 23/√22.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Let $p=⟨4,1,4⟩$ and $q=⟨2,3,3⟩.$ Find the scalar projection of $p$ onto $q.$
after.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the scalar projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{q}\,p & =\frac{p\cdot q}{|\,q\,|} \\  & =\frac{{p}_{x}{q}_{x}+{p}_{y}{q}_{y}+{p}_{z}{q}_{z}}{\sqrt{{q}_{x}^{2}+{q}_{y}^{2}+{q}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{4\cdot 2+1\cdot 3+4\cdot 3}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{3}^{2}+{3}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{23}{\sqrt{22}}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the scalar projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{|\,b\,|} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{\sqrt{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{(-1)\cdot 4+2\cdot 3+\sqrt{11}\cdot \sqrt{11}}{\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{3}^{2}+(\sqrt{11})^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{13}{\sqrt{36}} \\  & =\frac{13}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{a}\,b & =\frac{b\cdot a}{|\,a\,|} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{\sqrt{{a}_{x}^{2}+{a}_{y}^{2}+{a}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{13}{\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}+(\sqrt{11})^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{13}{\sqrt{16}} \\  & =\frac{13}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{b}\,a-{\text{comp}}_{a}\,b & =\frac{13}{6}-\frac{13}{4} \\  & =13(\frac{1}{6}-\frac{1}{4}) \\  & =13(\frac{2}{12}-\frac{3}{12}) \\  & =-\frac{13}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: Let $p=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 5\end{aligned}]$ and $q=[\begin{aligned}15 \\ \sqrt{2} \\ x\end{aligned}].$ Given that the scalar projection of $p$ onto $q$ is $0,$ find the value of $x.$
after.worked_solution:
Since $p$ is a nonzero vector, its scalar projection onto another nonzero vector $q$ equals zero only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
p⊥q\,⟹\,p\cdot q=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & ={p}_{x}\cdot {q}_{x}+{p}_{y}\cdot {q}_{y}+{p}_{z}\cdot {q}_{z} \\  & =(-2)\cdot 15+0\cdot \sqrt{2}+5\cdot x \\  & =5x-30.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & =0 \\ 5x-30 & =0 \\ 5x & =30 \\ x & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: Let $p=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ x \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ and $q=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].$ Given that the scalar projection of $p$ onto $q$ is $0,$ find the value of $x.$
after.worked_solution:
Since $p$ is a nonzero vector, its scalar projection onto another nonzero vector $q$ equals zero only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
p⊥q\,⟹\,p\cdot q=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & ={p}_{x}\cdot {q}_{x}+{p}_{y}\cdot {q}_{y}+{p}_{z}\cdot {q}_{z} \\  & =5\cdot 4+x\cdot (-2)+2\cdot (-3) \\  & =14-2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & =0 \\ 14-2x & =0 \\ 2x & =14 \\ x & =7.\end{aligned}
$$
